wu: Warm-up: 'I Spy' with jobs flashcards. Teacher holds up a job flashcard (e.g., 'teacher') and says 'I spy someone who helps students learn.' Students guess 'Is it a teacher?' Teacher responds 'Yes, it is! What does a teacher do?' Students say 'A teacher teaches.'
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Jobs Charades' - students act out a job and others guess 'Is he a doctor?' 'Does she drive a bus?'
Alternative 2: 'Jobs Pictionary' - students draw a job and others guess 'Is it a cook?'
pres: Presentation: Show 5 job flashcards (doctor, teacher, farmer, builder, cook). Model 'What does a doctor do?' 'A doctor helps sick people.' Ask 'What does a farmer do?' Students respond 'A farmer grows food.' Check understanding with 'Who helps sick people?' 'Who grows food?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a short story about a boy who wants to be a firefighter. Ask 'What does a firefighter do?'
Alternative 2: Bring in toy props (stethoscope, book, seeds, hammer, spoon) and ask 'What does this person do?'
prac: Guided practice: 'Jobs Guessing Game' in teams. Team A describes a job without naming it (e.g., 'They wear a uniform. They drive a big red truck. They help people.') Team B guesses 'Is it a firefighter?' Teacher monitors and helps with sentence starters 'They... ' 'They can... '
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Match the Job to the Tool' - students match flashcards (doctor-stethoscope, builder-hammer) and say 'A doctor uses a stethoscope.'
Alternative 2: 'Jobs Bingo' - students listen to descriptions and mark the job on their bingo card
ls: Listening slot: 'Jobs Listening Test' - students listen to 5 short audio clips (e.g., 'I work in a hospital. I help people feel better.') and write the job (doctor, teacher, etc.) on a worksheet. Teacher plays clips twice and checks answers.
re: Reactivation game: 'Jobs Relay Race' - two lines of students. Teacher shows a job flashcard, first student runs to the board, writes the job, runs back, tags next student. Team with all jobs written first wins.
prod: Production task: 'My Best Work Presentation' - students show their favorite project from the year (e.g., a poster, a story) and say 'This is my poster. I drew a teacher. She teaches students. I like this work.' Then they ask friends 'What is your best work?'
rw: Reading and writing slot: 'I Can... Statements' - students complete a certificate page by writing 5 sentences like 'I can read a short story.' 'I can write 3 sentences about my job.' Then they draw a picture of their favorite job.
st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Sing 'The People in Your Neighborhood' song (Sesame Street). Teacher says 'Today we celebrate Labour Day! Thank you to all workers.' Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students act out a job and others guess 'Is it a doctor?'
Students draw a job and others guess 'Is it a cook?'
Students race to write jobs on the board
Students write their skills and get a sticker
Students make cards for workers they know
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 sentences about a job they want to do in the future
Support: Trace the job names and draw a picture with teacher help
hw: Homework 1: Draw one job you love and write 3 sentences about it (e.g., 'I love being a teacher. I teach students. I help them learn.')
Homework 2: Ask your family about their jobs and write them down
Homework 3: Review your notes for the final assessment week
tip: Use Labour Day to connect to local Moroccan workers (e.g., farmers, builders) and discuss how they help the community. This makes the lesson culturally relevant and meaningful.
checklist: I can say 5 jobs in English
I can ask 'What does a ... do?'
I can present my best work
I can write 3 sentences about a job
I can read a short text about jobs
I can complete the I Can... certificate
